title: Fintechs top banks and stablecoins for cheap cross-border payment - BIS research
summary: Cross-border payments remain slow and expensive but fintech outfits such as Wise and Remitly have substantially cut costs relative to traditional retail bank wires while stabelcoins still suffer from issues with friction, according to BIS research.
content: Recent research from the Bank for International Settlements reveals that fintech companies like Wise and Remitly offer significantly cheaper cross-border payments than traditional retail banks. While cross-border transactions have historically been slow and costly, these fintech firms have successfully reduced costs. Meanwhile, stablecoins still encounter friction issues that hinder their efficiency for international money transfers.
content_ta: சர்வதேச அளவில் பணப் பரிமாற்றம் செய்ய பாரம்பரிய வங்கிகளை விட Wise மற்றும் Remitly போன்ற fintech நிறுவனங்கள் மிகவும் குறைந்த கட்டணத்தை வசூலிப்பதாக BIS நடத்திய புதிய ஆராய்ச்சியில் தெரியவந்துள்ளது. சர்வதேச பணப் பரிமாற்றங்கள் பொதுவாக மெதுவாகவும் செலவு மிக்கதாகவும் இருந்த நிலையில், இந்த நிறுவனங்கள் கட்டணங்களை வெற்றிகரமாகக் குறைத்துள்ளன. இதற்கிடையில், stablecoins இன்னும் சில நடைமுறைச் சிக்கல்களை எதிர்கொண்டு வருவதாக அந்த ஆய்வில் குறிப்பிடப்பட்டுள்ளது.

content: Solana has launched its most significant network upgrade since 2020. The new voting system is designed to achieve settlement times of approximately 150 milliseconds. content_ta: 2020-ம் ஆண்டிற்குப் பிறகு Solana-வின் மிகப்பெரிய நெட்வொர்க் மேம்படுத்தல் வெளியிடப்பட்டுள்ளது. புதிய வோட்டிங் சிஸ்டம் மூலம் பரிவர்த்தனைகள் சுமார் 150 மில்லி விநாடிகளுக்குள் முடிக்க இலக்கு நிர்ணயிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. இதனால் பேமெண்ட்டுகள் மற்றும் டெபாசிட்களுக்கான காத்திருப்பு நேரம் குறையும். பயனர்கள் தங்களின் பழைய வாலெட்டுகளை மாற்றாமல் தொடர்ந்து பயன்படுத்தலாம்.

title: XRP Ledger bug fix moved to November after validator support dipped for two hours
summary:
The delay in the XRP Ledger bug fix may heighten market uncertainty, affecting confidence and price momentum for XRP in the near term.
The post XRP Ledger bug fix delayed to November after validator support dip appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: The rollout of a crucial bug fix for the XRP Ledger has been postponed to November. This delay occurred after validator support experienced a brief dip for two hours. Industry observers note that the postponement could introduce short-term market uncertainty and potentially impact price momentum for XRP as investors await the rescheduled deployment.
content_ta: XRP Ledger-ல் உள்ள ஒரு முக்கியமான பிழை திருத்தத்தை நவம்பர் மாதத்திற்கு ஒத்திவைத்துள்ளனர். இரண்டு மணி நேரம் வேலிடேட்டர் ஆதரவு குறைந்ததைத் தொடர்ந்து இந்த தாமதம் ஏற்பட்டுள்ளது. இந்தத் தாமதம் சந்தையில் குறுகிய கால நிச்சயமற்ற தன்மையை ஏற்படுத்தக்கூடும் என்றும், இது XRP-இன் விலை ஏற்ற இறக்கங்களை பாதிக்கலாம் என்றும் நிபுணர்கள் கருதுகின்றனர்.

title: Bitcoin gives back its run at $85,000 as Tesla and Meta fail to calm AI nerves
summary: BTC broke through its $84,000 ceiling late Wednesday, then slid back to the $82,500 support analysts are watching as tech futures fell.
content: Bitcoin recently fell back after attempting to reach $85,000, sliding to around the $82,500 support level. The drop followed a decline in tech futures, as major technology companies like Tesla and Meta struggled to calm investor anxieties regarding artificial intelligence.
content_ta: $85,000 மதிப்பை எட்ட முயன்ற Bitcoin, அதன் பிறகு சரிவைச் சந்தித்து $82,500 என்ற ஆதரவு நிலைக்கு அருகில்தள்ளப்பட்டது. தொழில்நுட்ப துறை எதிர்கால ஒப்பந்தங்கள் குறைந்ததாலும், AI குறித்த முதலீட்டாளர்களின் அச்சத்தைப் போக்க Tesla மற்றும் Meta போன்ற முன்னணி தொழில்நுட்ப நிறுவனங்கள் தவறியதாலும் இந்த விலை சரிவு ஏற்பட்டது.

title: Move over memecoins: Crypto ‘meme games’ coming, bagholders and all
summary: “Plenty will be ponzis. Plenty will get exploited. Plenty will insta die. There will be ridiculous gains, and people will get absolutely f***ing rinsed,” says Illuvium co-founder Kieran Warwick.
content: Crypto meme games are emerging as a new trend in the digital asset space, following the popularity of memecoins. Industry figures warn that while these upcoming games could generate massive gains for some participants, they also carry severe risks. Observers note that many projects may fail, suffer exploits, or turn out to be unsustainable schemes, leading to significant financial losses for investors.
content_ta: Memecoins-ன் வெற்றigaiத் தொடர்ந்து, கிரிப்டோ சந்தையில் புதிய 'meme games' வரவிருக்கின்றன. இந்த புதிய கேம்களில் சிலருக்கு அபரிமிதமான லாபம் கிடைக்கலாம் என்றாலும், இதில் பல ஆபத்துக்களும் இருப்பதாக துறை வல்லுநர்கள் எச்சரிக்கின்றனர். பல திட்டங்கள் தோல்வியடையலாம், ஹேக்கிங் தாக்குதல்களுக்கு ஆளாகலாம் அல்லது நீண்ட காலம் நீடிக்காமல் போகலாம், இதனால் முதலீட்டாளர்களுக்கு பெரும் நிதி இழப்பு ஏற்படும் அபாயம் உள்ளது.

title: OCC waiver rule puts active stablecoin issuers on notice
summary:
Existing US issuers awaiting OCC approval need discretionary relief to keep issuing from Jan. 18, 2027; filing alone is insufficient.
Read the full story on CryptoSlate
Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox
tags: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
content: A new waiver rule from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency places active stablecoin issuers under strict notice. Existing US issuers waiting for approval require discretionary relief to continue issuing tokens past January 18, 2027. Simply filing an application will not be enough to meet the regulatory requirements, signaling a tighter oversight approach for digital asset companies operating within the country.
content_ta: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency-இன் புதிய விலக்கு விதி active stablecoin வழங்குநர்களை கடுமையான எச்சரிக்கைக்குள்ளாக்கியுள்ளது. ஒப்புதலுக்காகக் காத்திருக்கும் US வழங்குநர்கள், ஜனவரி 18, 2027-க்குப் பிறகும் தொடர்ந்து வழங்குவதற்கு விருப்பப் பிரிவு நிவாரணம் பெற வேண்டும். விண்ணப்பம் மட்டும் தாக்கல் செய்வது போதாது.

title: Why XRP May Retest $1 Before Its Next Major Rally: Analyst
summary: XRP's recovery rests on weekly closes above $1.33; failure to regain that level leaves the $1 region exposed, an analyst warned today.
content: An analyst warns that XRP could retest the $1 price region if it fails to secure weekly closes above $1.33. The cryptocurrency's potential for a major rally depends heavily on reclaiming this crucial technical level. Without it, the market may see a deeper correction before any upward momentum resumes.
content_ta: எதிர்வரும் வாரங்களில் XRP-ன் விலை $1.33-க்கு மேல் நிலைபெறத் தவறினால், அது மீண்டும் $1 பகுதியை சோதிக்க நேரிடும் என்று ஒரு ஆய்வாளர் எச்சரித்துள்ளார். இந்த முக்கிய எல்லையை மீட்டு எடுத்தால் மட்டுமே அடுத்த கட்ட முன்னேற்றம் சாத்தியமாகும் என்றும் தெரிவிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: How did PYTH’s price fall for bears’ trap after latest surge?
summary: Rising short positions in the perpetual market put the price at risk.
content: Following a recent price surge, PYTH experienced a sharp fall that experts warn may be a trap for bears. Market data indicates an increase in rising short positions within the perpetual market, which has placed the cryptocurrency's price at significant risk of further downward pressure and volatility in the near term.
content_ta: சமீபத்திய விலை உயர்வைத் தொடர்ந்து, PYTH விலை திடீரென சரிந்துள்ளது. இது கரடிகளின் (bears) பொறிதலாக இருக்கலாம் என்று நிபுணர்கள் எச்சரிக்கின்றனர். பெர்பச்சுவல் சந்தையில் குறுகிய நிலைப்பாடுகள் (short positions) அதிகரித்து வருவதாக சந்தை தரவுகள் காட்டுகின்றன. இதனால் PYTH விலை மேலும் வீழ்ச்சியடையும் அபாயம் ஏற்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: NEAR sees major gains after new governance proposal — Can it stay above $5?
summary: Do Spot NEAR ETF outflows pose a threat to the altcoin's upward trajectory?
content: NEAR recently recorded significant gains following the introduction of a new governance proposal. As the altcoin climbs, analysts are questioning whether it can maintain its position above the $5 price level. At the same time, market participants are monitoring potential risks, such as Spot NEAR ETF outflows, to determine if they could threaten the cryptocurrency's ongoing upward trajectory.
content_ta: புதிய governance proposal அறிமுகப்படுத்தப்பட்டதைத் தொடர்ந்து NEAR குறிப்பிடத்தக்க gains-ஐ பதிவு செய்துள்ளது. இந்த altcoin உயர்ந்து வருவதால், அது $5 விலை நிலைக்கு மேல் தனது நிலையைத் தக்கவைக்க முடியுமா என்று analysts கேள்வி எழுப்புகின்றனர். அதே நேரத்தில், Spot NEAR ETF outflows போன்ற சாத்தியமான risks cryptocurrency-யின் மேல்நோக்கிய பயணத்திற்கு அச்சுறுத்தலாக இருக்க முடியுமா என்பதை market participants உன்னிப்பாகக் கவனித்து வருகின்றனர்.

title: Why Is Lighter Up 23% This Week? 2 Catalysts Explain the Move
summary:

title: Circle CEO Shrugs Off Bitcoin's Slump and Pitches Digital Dollars for the AI Era
summary:
Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire shrugs off Bitcoin's slump and pitches digital dollars for AI payments as GENIUS Act rules near.
The post Circle CEO Shrugs Off Bitcoin's Slump and Pitches Digital Dollars for the AI Era appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire remains unconcerned by Bitcoin's recent market slump, instead focusing on the potential of digital dollars. As new legislative rules approach, Allaire is actively pitching the use of digital currencies for payments in the emerging artificial intelligence era.
content_ta: Circle நிறுவனத்தின் CEO Jeremy Allaire, Bitcoin-ன் சந்தை வீழ்ச்சியைக் குறித்து கவலைப்படவில்லை. மாறாக, வரவிருக்கும் புதிய சட்ட விதிகளின் அடிப்படையில், செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு (AI) யுகத்தில் பணப்பரிவர்த்தனைகளுக்கு டிஜிட்டல் டாலர்களைப் பயன்படுத்துவதை அவர் பரிந்துரைக்கிறார்.

title: Nokia beats profit estimates as AI data center demand surges
summary:
Nokia's strategic pivot to AI and cloud markets highlights its adaptability, but reliance on major cloud clients poses potential risks.
The post Nokia beats profit estimates as AI data center demand surges appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Nokia surpassed profit expectations, driven by a surge in demand for AI data centers. This highlights the company's successful strategic shift toward artificial intelligence and cloud markets. However, analysts note that a heavy reliance on a few major cloud clients could introduce potential risks moving forward.
content_ta: AI டேட்டா சென்டர்களின் தேவை அதிகரித்ததன் காரணமாக Nokia நிறுவனத்தின் லாபம் எதிர்பார்த்ததை விட அதிகமாக உள்ளது. செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு மற்றும் கிளவுட் சந்தைகளை நோக்கி இந்நிறுவனம் வெற்றிகரமாக மாறியுள்ளதை இது காட்டுகிறது. இருப்பினும், சில முக்கிய கிளவுட் வாடிக்கையாளர்களை மட்டுமே நம்பியிருப்பது எதிர்காலத்தில் ஆபத்தை ஏற்படுத்தக்கூடும் என்று ஆய்வாளர்கள் குறிப்பிடுகின்றனர்.

title: Bitcoin treasury companies return to profit as prices exceed $80K
summary:
The cautious approach of treasury firms amid Bitcoin's price surge highlights market volatility and strategic shifts in corporate crypto investments.

content: Bitcoin treasury companies have returned to profitability as Bitcoin prices exceeded $80,000. This milestone highlights a period of strategic shifts and cautious management among corporate crypto investors navigating ongoing market volatility.

title: Noetix Robotics files confidentially for Hong Kong IPO to raise hundreds of millions
summary:
Noetix Robotics' IPO could significantly impact the robotics market by democratizing access to affordable humanoid technology globally.

content: Noetix Robotics has confidentially filed for an initial public offering in Hong Kong, aiming to raise hundreds of millions of dollars. The anticipated public listing could significantly impact the global robotics market by expanding access to affordable humanoid technology.
content_ta: Noetix Robotics நிறுவனம் Hong Kong-ல் தனது ஆரம்ப பொதுப் பங்கு வெளியீட்டுக்காக (IPO) இரகசியமாக விண்ணப்பித்துள்ளது. இதன் மூலம் பல மில்லியன் டாலர்களை திரட்ட இலக்கு நிர்ணயித்துள்ளது. இந்த புதிய பப்ளிக் லிஸ்டிங் உலகளாவிய ரோபாட்டிக்ஸ் சந்தையில் பெரிய தாக்கத்தை ஏற்படுத்தும்.

title: Trump visits South Carolina to rally support for Sen. Darline Graham
summary:
Trump's support for Graham may strengthen Republican unity, potentially altering voter dynamics and impacting the South Carolina Senate race.

content: Trump recently traveled to South Carolina to rally support for Sen. Darline Graham. This political visit aims to strengthen Republican unity and could significantly impact voter dynamics in the upcoming Senate race within the region.
content_ta: செனட்டர் Darline Graham-க்கு ஆதர திரட்டுவதற்காக Trump சமீபத்தில் South Carolina-விற்கு பயணம் மேற்கொண்டார். இந்த அரசியல் பயணம் குடியரசுக் கட்சியின் ஒற்றுமையை வலுப்படுத்துவதோடு, அந்தப் பகுதியில் வரவிருக்கும் செனட் தேர்தலின் வாக்காளர் இயக்கவியலையும் கணிசமாகப் பாதிக்கும்.

title: Trump taps heating oil reserve to curb prices before 2026 midterms
summary:
Releasing oil reserves may sway voter sentiment, impacting Senate races and highlighting energy policy's role in political strategy.

content: Recent Bitcoin price movements indicate that extreme social media sentiment often signals market turning points. Data from Santiment shows that retail optimism on platforms like X, Reddit, and Telegram peaked on September 20, leading to a downward turn for BTC. Conversely, peak fear and bearish commentary reached their highest levels on October 15, which ultimately marked the market bottom before a reversal.
content_ta: சமீபத்திய Bitcoin விலை நகர்வுகள், சமூக வலைப்பதளங்களின் தீவிரமான மனநிலை பெரும்பாலும் சந்தையின் திருப்புமுனைகளைக் குறிக்கிறது என்பதைக் காட்டுகின்றன. Santiment-ன் தரவுகளின்படி, X, Reddit மற்றும் Telegram போன்ற தளங்களில் சில்லறை முதலீட்டாளர்களின் நம்பிக்கை செப்டம்பர் 20 அன்று உச்சத்தை அடைந்தது, இது BTC விலையில் சரிவை ஏற்படுத்தியது. மாறாக, அக்டோபர் 15 அன்று உச்சக்கட்ட அச்சமும் கரடி சந்தை (bearish) கருத்துகளும் மிக உயர்ந்த நிலையை அடைந்தன, இது இறுதியில் சந்தையின் வீழ்ச்சியின் அடிப்பகுதியைக் குறித்தது.

title: Bitcoin Has New Major Advantage Over Gold, Analyst Says
summary: Analyst Jesse Eckel argues that Bitcoin has a major scarcity advantage over gold as scientists make progress toward artificially producing the precious metal.
content: Analyst Jesse Eckel suggests that Bitcoin holds a significant scarcity advantage over gold. title: GRVT Burns 1.1 Million Tokens as Countdown to Grvt 2.0 Begins
summary: The discretionary buyback represents close to 1% of circulating supply and precedes four planned product milestones culminating in Grvt 2.0. Road Town, British Virgin Islands, October 22, 2026 – Grvt, a self-custodial trading platform built on its own zero-knowledge (ZK) chain, announced that the Foundation’s token issuer has completed its first GRVT token buyback, purchasing and burning 1.1 million GRVT tokens on the open market. The transaction permanently removed close to 1% of GRVT’s circulating supply at the time of purchase. It marks the first of five milestones ahead of the planned launch of Grvt 2.0 at the end of November 2026.   A discretionary buyback with on-chain verification The Foundation’s token issuer intends to conduct further buybacks on a monthly basis. Each transaction remains entirely at the issuer’s discretion, with no predetermined purchase amount or guaranteed schedule. Buybacks are executed through an independent execution partner, with purchased tokens transferred to a designated burn address and permanently removed from circulation. The transactions can be independently verified through the public buyback dashboard, which records the number of tokens purchased and burned, the percentage of circulating supply represented, cumulative burns and on-chain transaction hashes. “The GRVT token is an important part of the ecosystem we are building,” said Hong, co-founder and CEO of Grvt. “We welcome the issuer’s buybacks as a demonstration of its long-term commitment to the ecosystem and community. Grvt is expanding its products and markets, and the issuer’s buybacks sit alongside that as a supportive mechanism aimed at reducing circulating token supply.” Grvt outlines four product milestones The announcement follows GRVT’s token generation event in July 2026 and precedes a series of planned launches. Grvt Earn, scheduled for the end of October, will introduce yield opportunities backed by tokenized fixed-income assets, with target yields of up to 11%. Returns are expected to derive from underlying asset cash flows, including interest, premiums and invoice-related income. Asset-supplying partners will be announced at launch. Target yields are not guaranteed. Stable Funding Perps, scheduled for November, will introduce perpetual futures linked to commodities, stocks, foreign exchange and indices. The contracts are planned to carry zero trading fees and use once-daily funding. Grvt aims to list more than 1,000 markets by the end of December 2026. Yield as Margin, also scheduled for November, will allow eligible Grvt Earn balances to support trading positions while continuing to accrue yield, subject to applicable product terms and risk parameters. Grvt 2.0, scheduled for the end of November, will consolidate these capabilities into a single self-custodial app, alongside a new name, visual identity and the company’s 2027 roadmap. Addressing idle capital The expansion follows a survey of Grvt traders conducted earlier in 2026. Six in ten respondents reported keeping at least a quarter of their capital on the platform idle, while many reported moving funds elsewhere to pursue yields of 8% or more. Grvt’s upcoming products aim to reduce the separation between earning yield and deploying capital for trading. “Traders shouldn’t have to choose between putting their capital to work and keeping it ready to trade,” Hong said. “Grvt 2.0 is designed around a single self-custodial balance that can support both activities.” Founded in 2022, Grvt currently supports perpetual futures across approximately 200 cryptocurrency and real-world asset markets. The GRVT token launched in July 2026 and confers no ownership, profit or other economic rights. Further details are available in the full announcement. About Grvt Grvt is a self-custodial trading platform operating on its own zero-knowledge chain. The platform supports cryptocurrency and real-world asset perpetual futures and is developing products that allow eligible balances to earn yield while supporting trading activity. Learn more at grvt.io. Media contact Lesner Head of Marketing, Grvt lesner.chua@grvt.io

This move marks the first of five major product milestones leading up to the planned launch of Grvt 2.0 at the end of November 2026, which aims to consolidate new yield and trading features into a single app.

title: Layer 2 Scaling Solutions
summary:
Layer 2 scaling solutions help blockchains like Ethereum process more activity without forcing every transaction to happen directly on the base chain.
Ethereum’s main network is secure and decentralized, but blockspace is limited. When demand rises, fees increase and users can get priced out. Layer 2s address this by moving transaction activity to scaling systems that sit around Ethereum while still using it for settlement, security, data posting, or verification.
The most important Layer 2 designs today are rollups. Rollups process transactions off-chain, bundle them together, and post data or proofs back to Ethereum. This makes transactions cheaper and faster while keeping a connection to Ethereum’s trust foundation.
content: Layer 2 scaling solutions help blockchains like Ethereum process more transactions by moving activity off the main network. When demand rises, base chain fees increase. Layer 2 systems, particularly rollups, handle transactions separately and post the results back to Ethereum. This approach keeps transactions fast and affordable while utilizing Ethereum for security and settlement.
content_ta: Layer 2 scaling solutions போன்ற தொழில்நுட்பங்கள் Ethereum போன்ற blockchains-ல் அதிகப்படியான பரிவர்த்தனைகளைச் செயல்படுத்த உதவுகின்றன. main network-ல் தேவைகள் அதிகரிக்கும்போது கட்டணங்கள் உயர்வதால், Rollups போன்ற Layer 2 அமைப்புகள் பரிவர்த்தனைகளை தனியாகக் கையாண்டு பாதுகாப்பிற்காக Ethereum-ஐப் பயன்படுத்துகின்றன. இதனால் பரிவர்த்தனைகள் வேகமாகவும் மலிவாகவும் நடைபெறுகின்றன.

content: Chinese prosecutors have initiated legal proceedings in Tianjin to confiscate $5.1 billion in Bitcoin that was previously seized by authorities in the United Kingdom during the Qian case. A court hearing is scheduled following a mandatory notice period. Meanwhile, a separate legal battle regarding the ownership of the same cryptocurrency assets is ongoing in London.
content_ta: Tianjin நீதிமன்றத்தில் Chinese prosecutors சார்பில் Qian வழக்கில் UK அதிகாரிகளால் பறிமுதல் செய்யப்பட்ட $5.1B மதிப்பிலான Bitcoin-ஐ அரசுடமையாக்க கோரி வழக்கு தொடரப்பட்டுள்ளது. ஆறு மாத அறிவிப்பு காலத்திற்கு பிறகு இந்த மனு விசாரணைக்கு வரவுள்ளது. இதற்கிடையில், இதே cryptocurrency மீதான உரிமை கோரும் மற்றொரு வழக்கு London-ல் நடந்து வருகிறது.

title: Solana targets faster finality, while Wall Street cuts the cash that must move
summary:

Under the new protocol, confirmed and finalized become the same state. At the National Securities Clearing Corporation (NSCC), multilateral netting cuts the value of equities payment obligations by an average of…

Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox
content: Solana has activated the Alpenglow upgrade on its mainnet, replacing TowerBFT to target a faster finality time of about 150 milliseconds, merging confirmed and finalized states. Meanwhile, at the National Securities Clearing Corporation, multilateral netting is reducing the volume of equities payment obligations, streamlining capital movement for traditional financial markets.
content_ta: Solana தனது mainnet-ல் Alpenglow அப்ரேடை இயக்கியுள்ளது. இது TowerBFT-க்கு பதிலாக சுமார் 1 இதழ் நொடிகள் அல்லது 150 மில்லி விநாடிகளில் இறுதி நிலையை (finality) எட்ட இலக்கு நிர்ணயிக்கிறது. இதற்கிடையில், National Securities Clearing Corporation-ல் மல்டிலேட்ரல் நெட்டிங் மூலம் பங்குச் சந்தை பணப் பரிமாற்றக் கடப்பாடுகள் குறைக்கப்படுகின்றன.

title: MEXC’s New-Token Trading Volume Rises 77% in September as Stock-Related Trading Expands Into On-Chain New-Token Markets
summary: Mutsamudu, Comoros, October 22, 2026 – MEXC, a pioneer in 0-fee digital asset trading, has released its September trading data. New-token and TradFi spot trading volumes rose 77% and 78% month over month, respectively, while tokenized U.S. stock trading volume increased 81%. Stock Meme projects also took the top two spots by new-token spot trading volume, as stock-related trading expanded into on-chain new-token markets.   In September, the number of newly listed tokens on MEXC increased 15% month over month, while the number of users trading new tokens grew 27%. Seven of the top 10 new tokens by spot trading volume made their exchange debut on MEXC, highlighting the platform’s coverage of trending early-stage assets. Stock Meme projects 4STOCK and MEMEROBINHOOD together accounted for approximately 38% of the top 10’s combined trading volume, underscoring the activity around stock-related themes in new-token trading.   Beyond stock-themed meme tokens, tokenized stocks are also being used as quote assets for on-chain new token trading pairs. Four Stock Meme projects, including MEMEROBINHOOD, SI, MOO, and 4STOCK, ranked among the top 10 gainers. Together, they accounted for approximately 67% of the ranking’s total trading volume. EMBER and BREW, two tokens associated with token launch platforms, also ranked among the top 10 new tokens by spot trading volume. Both platforms support trading pairs between new tokens and stock-related assets. These developments suggest that the convergence of stocks and crypto assets is moving beyond stock tokenization into a broader range of on-chain trading use cases. Of the five distinct Stock Meme projects that appeared across the two rankings this month, three run on Robinhood Chain, an emerging public blockchain.   Echoing activity in the new-token market, MEXC’s tokenized U.S. stock trading volume rose 81% month over month in September, accounting for approximately 66% of the increase in TradFi spot trading volume. Growth extended beyond a handful of assets: more than half of the tokenized U.S. stocks saw their trading volumes at least double. The number of tokenized U.S. stocks in the top 10 by TradFi spot trading volume rose from three in August to five in September. MRVL and META entered the ranking, with trading volumes up 212% and 152%, respectively.   Circle-related trading activity also appeared across both MEXC’s tokenized U.S. stock and new-token markets. On September 16, Circle launched the mainnet of its own blockchain, Arc. ARGUS, the token of a launch platform on Arc, was listed on MEXC the same day and ranked among the month’s top 10 new tokens by spot trading volume. During the same month, trading volume for tokenized U.S. stock CRCL rose 103% month over month, placing it fourth by TradFi spot trading volume.   To drive user participation, MEXC held xStocks Gala, a tokenized U.S. stock trading campaign, in September. The campaign attracted nearly 100,000 registrations, with average daily trading volume exceeding $3.4 billion during the event. By combining popular assets with trading incentives, MEXC further lowered barriers to participation in the tokenized stock market.   MEXC CEO Vugar Usi said, “The convergence of stocks and crypto assets is changing how users participate in markets. A single market theme can drive trading activity in both tokenized U.S. stocks and on-chain new tokens. title: Moneybox Sets Out Six Policy Asks to Bring 7 Million More People Into Stocks and Shares ISAs by 2035
summary:
Moneybox, the award winning wealth management platform with over 2 million customers and £23 billion in assets under administration, has today launched a retail investing manifesto that sets out six key policy asks to take the UK from a nation of savers to a nation of confident investors. 
The manifesto, which was previewed at an exclusive event at One Great George Street on Wednesday 21st October, calls on the government to double down on making investing as easy as saving. If done correctly, the opportunity is significant: 7 million adults have £10,000 or more sitting in cash savings, the real-world illustration of findings from Moneybox’s 2026 Financial Confidence Index that shows confidence in investing (40%) significantly trails confidence in saving (83%). The manifesto argues that closing this confidence gap with practical, behavioural and product-led policy changes could help bring those savers into the stocks and shares ecosystem.
Brian Byrnes, Director of Personal Finance at Moneybox said: “The policy asks in our manifesto are designed to remove the structural and cultural barriers holding people back, creating a clear pathway to bring millions more people into stocks and shares ISAs by 2035. 
“We know that more of our friends, family, and the general public should be investing, and while great strides have been made with the democratisation of access thanks to technology, there is more that can and should be done to ensure people achieve the resilience and security that investing can bring.” 
The six policy asks outlined in the manifesto are:
Build on the success of the Lifetime ISA
Rather than creating new products from scratch, the government should build on the success of the Stocks and Shares Lifetime ISA, a government backed investment product that is growing in popularity every year.
Update the adviser charging rules
Review and modernise the adviser charging rules to allow for more innovative and accessible pricing models for advice, closing the advice gap and helping millions invest with greater confidence.
Launch government-backed investment funds
Establish a range of low-cost diversified funds with a home country bias (similar to Sweden's AP7 Såfa) to provide first-time investors with a clear, confident and sensible entry point to investing.  
Extend workplace auto-enrolment to saving and investing 
Extending workplace auto-enrolment to saving and investing accounts that employees are opted in to. This will remove friction and build long-term investing habits effortlessly.
Provide workplace investment and pension health checks
Make workplace investment and pension health checks more regular, more personalised and easier to access so savers and investors get reassurance that they’re on the right track.
Produce a 10-year retail investing strategy with a government champion
Appoint a dedicated government champion to unite fragmented oversight, establish shared goals, and lead a unified 10-year strategy to grow retail investment.
The launch of Moneybox’s retail investing manifesto also coincides with the 10th anniversary of the launch of its app. Drawing on those 10 years’ of experience, and insights from over 2 million customers, it believes these measures can broaden participation and build investing confidence nationwide.

title: Ondato and Trinsic Expand Digital Identity Verification Amid EUDI Transition
summary:
Ondato, a compliance technology provider offering an all-in-one platform for identity, risk, and customer journey across IDV/KYC, AML and age verification for regulated businesses, announces a partnership with Trinsic to verify their customers through digital identity. This partnership arrives at a critical time in the EU, as multiple member states roll out  EU Digital Identity Wallets under the European Digital Identity (EUDI) mandate. Trinsic will act as Ondato’s infrastructure provider behind the new digital identity capability.
According to eIDAS 2.0 (Regulation (EU) 2024/1183), all 27 EU member countries must offer at least one digital identity wallet to their citizens by the end of 2026. These digital wallets are designed as government-issued or government-recognised mobile apps that allow an individual to prove their identity and voluntarily share verified information about themselves when interacting with regulated businesses. By December 2027, banks, financial institutions and other regulated businesses that require strong user authentication will be required to accept these wallets when requested by users as a way to verify customers.
Ondato is expanding its capabilities now to prepare for this major development in European digital identity. This builds on the national digital identity methods Ondato already supports, such as Smart-ID. EUDI wallet-based verification will become part of Ondato’s larger customer intelligence platform. As with all of Ondato’s verification options, this functionality will feed into risk scoring, continuous fraud monitoring and detection, and optimising the entire customer journey.
Liudas Kanapienis, co-founder and CEO of Ondato, says, “EU digital identity wallets are the biggest change in a generation to how Europeans prove who they are. For many regulated businesses, accepting them won't be optional. With Trinsic, our clients can accept wallets as they launch, on the same platform they already use for verification, risk and monitoring. It's another step in our expansion as the intelligence layer between businesses and their customers, in Europe and beyond.”
Riley Hughes, CEO of Trinsic, says, “As the leading digital ID gateway for identity verification, Trinsic has been preparing for EUDI since the earliest phase of the mandate. We already support national identity authentication services for France, Italy, Denmark, Austria, and other member states. With this partnership, we’re providing the necessary technology backing for Ondato’s customers amidst the most important European digital ID mandate of the decade.”
Ondato’s EUDI wallet acceptance capabilities will live alongside its existing suite of identity verification and KYC methods. Using Ondato, businesses will continue to utilise a robust roster of digital identity verification tools backed by continuous fraud protection, all available on a single comprehensive platform.

title: 85% of Travel Intermediaries Say FX Cost Is a Challenge, Despite Only One in Four Tracking This Cost
summary:
Modulr, the payments automation platform built to scale, has today revealed exclusive research highlighting the hidden cost of FX for travel intermediaries. The research reveals that, while 85% of travel intermediaries say FX cost is a challenge, only 26% track this cost precisely. 88% of respondents roughly estimate that it is more than €300,000 per year.
The research launches alongside Modulr’s new FX solution featuring account-to-account and virtual card currency exchange, so you can convert on demand with transparent, competitive rates as well as issuing virtual cards in your supplier's currency and funding from your primary balance.
Integrated directly into Modulr’s platform, this gives businesses a single place to convert balances, fund cross-currency card payments, and manage multi-currency operations, with no need for separate FX providers.
When fragmented FX becomes an operational problem
For businesses running multi-currency operations, FX has long meant a separate provider, a separate process, and a separate reconciliation trail, ultimately creating risk. Modulr’s new research, surveying 400 finance, treasury, and operations decision-makers at travel intermediaries across the UK and Western Europe, highlights the real cost of this risk. 93% of respondents, for example, say their business has paid to convert the same money twice, and only 5% have processes to stop it.
Only one third (32%) describe their FX as fully integrated, or handled automatically in the platform they use to pay suppliers. Treasury teams are spending more time managing disconnected systems than optimising payments operations. Costs are often hard to predict, and the burden compounds as transaction volume grows.
Modulr’s integrated FX solution addresses these challenges and reduces operational cost by handling conversion inside the same platform used for payments, accounts, and cards, creating a more automated and streamlined process. Rates are transparent, competitive with the mid-market rate, and consistent at weekends with no surcharge. Businesses pay only the exchange rate margin on each conversion, with no fixed or monthly fees.
Melek Pirgon, Chief Product Officer at Modulr, said: “For businesses scaling across currencies, FX can often mean friction, with a separate provider, a separate reconciliation process, and costs that are hard to predict. The research we have launched today highlights this, with just one quarter of businesses tracking the cost of FX despite 85% citing it as a challenge.
That is one of the key problems we are removing with our FX solution, built directly into the same platform our customers already use for automating payments. This means transparent and competitive rates as well as a full audit trail with no new system or stakeholders to manage. I’m excited to see how we build this offering out in the coming months, including offering booking-linked FX protection to ease the FX cost of booking margins for our customers.”
Looking ahead, Modulr will be expanding its FX solution to offer booking-linked FX protection, helping travel businesses secure exchange rates for future supplier payments and manage the impact of booking changes. By connecting hedging with virtual cards, account-to-account payments and reconciliation, the FX component of booking margins is made much more predictable.

title: Strategic Partnership With Ecommpay Gives Dolphin Dynamics’ Travel Clients Access to Global Payments Platform
summary:
Travel technology provider, Dolphin Dynamics, is working with inclusive global payments provider, Ecommpay, to provide its clients with access to the award-winning payment gateway for local and alternative payment methods in any currency. The strategic partnership also allows travel agents, tour operators and travel management companies (TMCs) to benefit from Ecommpay’s risk and authorisation tooling.
UK-based Dolphin Dynamics provides travel businesses with an integrated suite of CRM, reservations, back-office and booking-engine software designed to reduce daily administration and streamline operational processes. Its platform provides a central environment for managing bookings and associated operational and financial processes. Working with tour operators, leisure travel agencies and TMCs, from independents to multinational corporations, Dolphin Dynamics supports businesses in more than 15 countries.
Through the strategic partnership, Dolphin Dynamics integrates Ecommpay’s payment capabilities with its travel technology platform. Customers completing a payment are directed to Ecommpay’s hosted payment page, where payment information is entered and processed within Ecommpay’s environment. Dolphin then uses Ecommpay’s API to retrieve the payment status, update the booking accordingly and register the payment.
By linking payment activity back into Dolphin, payment status can be reflected within the booking workflow and the corresponding payment registered in Dolphin, helping connect the customer payment journey with the wider booking management process.
“Our aim is to simplify back-office processes for our travel clients, ensuring every stage of the customer journey runs smoothly and without friction,” said Chuck Richardson, Managing Director at Dolphin Dynamics. “To achieve this goal, we carefully select specialists that will deliver fit for purpose solutions.
“Ecommpay delivers secure and accessible payments across borders and in all currencies, allowing our clients’ customers to pay using their preferred payment methods. This boosts conversions and profitability by increasing confidence and convenience and supports a positive booking experience, from research to booking confirmation.”
Roy Blokker of Ecommpay added: “This partnership deepens our footprint within the travel and hospitality sector, where we work with specialist travel-tech providers who need affordable access to multi-currency acceptance and conversion. Our inclusive and accessible payments platform ensures all payments are secure and compliant, regardless of region or currency.
“Dolphin Dynamics helps travel operators of all sizes to optimise processes and grow sales by streamlining back-office systems, and now the payment stage of the checkout journey can run as smoothly as the rest of the experience, without adding complexity for the travel operator.”

title: Mastercard Expands First-Party Trust Program to Help European Merchants From Rising “Friendly” Fraud
summary:
Mastercard today announced the expansion of its First-Party Trust program across Europe, to address the growing trend in first-party fraud, often referred to as ‘friendly’ fraud. This occurs when a cardholder disputes a legitimate purchase, either intentionally or because they do not recognize the transaction on their statement.
Global chargeback volume is predicted to reach 324 million transactions in 2028, a double-digit increase over the 2025 forecast of 261 million1. As digital commerce continues to grow across Europe, merchants and issuers face increasing pressure to manage disputes efficiently while accurately distinguishing genuine fraud from legitimate purchases.
Mastercard’s First-Party Trust program is designed to support this effort by increasing transaction transparency, through risk model-driven insights to inform authorization decisioning and merchant-provided evidence to assist issuers in reviewing disputed transactions. European issuers will be able to make more informed dispute decisions by more accurately distinguishing third-party fraud from first-party fraud.
How It Works
The First-Party Trust program aims to create greater transaction transparency between issuers and merchants, by giving merchants, including small businesses, the opportunity to submit pertinent insights to counter first-party fraud.
Mastercard provides two paths for the sharing of these enhanced insights between a merchant and card issuer. Merchants can send the insights directly as part of the transaction, or they can do so as part of the disputes process. The program enhances the resolution of such disputes by providing:
First Party Trust insights in authorization, powered by Mastercard fraud models, to help issuers separate third-party fraud, where someone's card details are used without their consent, from first-party fraud. Issuers get fraud-risk signals that point to likely third-party fraud and flag the transactions with the highest levels of trust;
Merchant-provided evidence that supports issuers assess the legitimacy of a disputed transaction, including information associated with the purchase, delivery, and authentication of the transaction, where available and appropriate;
New rules defining compelling evidence that can support issuers with the review of disputed purchases and reduce unnecessary chargebacks, including merchant chargeback protection for disputes that meet First-Party Trust evidence sharing requirements.
Michele Centemero, Executive Vice President, Services Europe, at Mastercard says: “As digital commerce continues to grow, building trust across the ecosystem has never been more important.  By helping merchants and issuers access relevant transaction information needed to review disputed purchases, we can reduce unnecessary disputes while strengthening confidence across the payments ecosystem.”
First-Party Trust is a global program that launched in the U.S., Canada, Latin America, the Caribbean, and across the Asia Pacific region in 2024. It will become available in Eastern Europe, Middle East and Africa in October 2026, and across Europe in July 2027.
NoYesPayments22 Oct, 2026
content: Mastercard has announced the expansion of its First-Party Trust program across Europe to help merchants combat rising first-party or friendly fraud. Set to launch in July 2027, the initiative increases transaction transparency by sharing risk model insights and merchant-provided evidence with issuers. This aims to help accurately distinguish genuine fraud from disputed legitimate purchases, reduce unnecessary chargebacks, and build greater trust across the digital payments ecosystem.

title: Businesses Expect AI to Manage Over a Third of Corporate Travel Spend by 2028, Worth an Estimated $700bn Globally
summary:
AI is expected to manage or authorise more than a third (37%) of corporate travel spend by 2028, equivalent to $700bn (£535bn) globally when applied to GBTA's 2025 business travel spending forecast. New research from Conferma, a global leader in virtual payment technology, reveals how businesses are preparing to give AI agents greater control over company money, extending their role from booking travel to managing payments.
Across the organisations surveyed, AI is expected to manage or authorise around 37% of corporate travel spend on average by 2028, while 28% expect agents to manage more than half of their travel budgets.
Controls surrounding agentic purchasing are developing more slowly. While 81% of organisations already have some form of policy, control or payment guardrail in place, only 36% describe those controls as comprehensive.
Mark Ledsham, CEO at Conferma, says, “Agentic spending authority is developing faster than the controls around it. Corporate travel could be one of the first proving grounds for agentic payments because it combines high transaction volumes, clear policies and significant spend.
Giving an AI agent authority over company money is very different from using AI to recommend a flight or hotel. Businesses need clear limits on what agents can spend, where they can spend it and when human intervention is required. The controls around those decisions must remain fixed, traceable and accountable.”
Larger travel programmes expect AI to take on more spend
The organisations managing the largest corporate travel budgets expect agents to take on the greatest share of spending. Those spending $6.8 million (£5 million) or more each year on corporate travel expect AI to manage around 51% of their travel spend by 2028, compared with around 27% among those spending less than $136,000 (£100,000).
More than half, 53%, of organisations spending $6.8 million (£5 million) or more say they already have comprehensive AI controls in place. 
As agents gain authority over larger pools of corporate spend, limits, supplier controls, monitoring and auditability become increasingly important.
Senior leaders are more confident than operational teams
Senior leaders are also substantially more willing to give AI autonomy. 86% of executive leaders and heads of department say they trust AI to manage travel bookings and spend, compared with 62% of travel and procurement decision-makers.
However, greater confidence does not mean fewer concerns. 69% of executive leaders and heads of department identify data security as a concern, compared with 59% of finance respondents and 38% across procurement and travel management. Businesses need greater alignment between leadership ambition and the operational controls required to support autonomous purchasing at scale.
Businesses are looking to put controls into the payment itself
Virtual cards rank highest for perceived security in AI-led corporate travel purchasing, selected by 30% of respondents, ahead of digital wallets at 21% and corporate cards and bank transfers at 19% each.
Among organisations with AI purchasing safeguards already in place, 55% require human approval before AI can complete a purchase, 51% use real-time monitoring, 49% apply spending limits and 37% currently use virtual cards with single-use or controlled spending limits.
Use of controlled virtual cards in this group is expected to rise from 37% to 48% by 2028, the biggest expected increase of any safeguard. As businesses prepare for greater agent autonomy, the findings indicate that attention is turning to payment methods that can carry spending rules into individual transactions.
Ledsham added, “As agents become more capable of acting independently, businesses need a way to delegate spending without handing over unrestricted financial authority. Payments can become part of that control layer. A controlled virtual card allows businesses to capture the speed and efficiency of agentic purchasing without removing the financial guardrails around the transaction. 
Corporate travel has the potential to be the testbed for how businesses will manage a much broader transition towards agentic commerce: giving AI enough authority to act while ensuring control over corporate money remains visible, enforceable and accountable.”

content: By 2028, businesses expect artificial intelligence to manage over a third of corporate travel spend globally, reaching an estimated $700bn. Research from Conferma highlights that while senior leaders are confident in granting AI greater purchasing autonomy, organizations are increasingly focusing on robust payment controls, such as virtual cards and spending limits, to ensure financial safety and accountability.

title: Ethereum’s four-minute settlement plan could lower the cost of moving crypto
summary: A new draft targets a fourfold cut in the time it takes Ethereum transactions to become final, which could free up money transfer services tie up while customers’ payments clear.
content: A new proposal for the Ethereum network aims to significantly reduce transaction finality times down to four minutes. By speeding up how quickly cryptocurrency transfers are settled, this fourfold reduction could lower operating costs and free up capital that money transfer services currently tie up while waiting for customer payments to clear.

title: Prism Data Raises $20 Million in Funding Amid Rapid Adoption of Its Cash Flow Underwriting Technology
summary:
After decades of relying primarily on traditional credit reports and scores, some of the largest and most sophisticated financial institutions in North America are rapidly adopting cash flow underwriting, a transformative approach to understanding creditworthiness based on consumers’ real-time banking history.
Traditional credit reports reveal little about how people earn, save, spend, or manage their money, leaving lenders with an incomplete picture of creditworthiness. The consequences are enormous: tens of billions of dollars are lost to defaults each year, while tens of millions of creditworthy consumers and small businesses remain shut out of mainstream credit or pay more than they should.
At Prism Data, we’ve spent more than ten years pioneering, proving, and deploying a better approach. Our founding insight was that data found within bank accounts, but beyond the four corners of a credit report, could materially improve lenders’ ability to assess risk across the credit spectrum, unlocking value for lenders, lowering costs for consumers, and expanding access to credit for the underserved.
What has surprised even us is the pace at which the market is now embracing cash flow underwriting.
Quietly, Prism has been leading this transformation.
Today, Prism works with three of the five largest fintech lenders in the United States and six of the ten largest digital banks. Prism’s technology is distributed through leading financial data and credit infrastructure providers like Equifax, Plaid, and LexisNexis. And we’re currently working with several of the country’s largest traditional banks to implement cash flow underwriting for millions more consumers and small businesses.
Our API volume tells the story of that widespread adoption. Over the past two years, the number of API requests banks and lenders have made for Prism solutions has increased more than 100x, representing an average compounded growth rate of more than 20% per month for two consecutive years. There is no better measure of how quickly cash flow underwriting has moved from the margins into the mainstream of lending.
These days, new models can be built faster than ever. Trust is a different story. 
The first CashScore® model was deployed for consumer credit decisioning by an FDIC-regulated financial institution in 2018. In the years since, it has been tested and used across hundreds of lending portfolios, comprising tens of billions of dollars in loan originations, and has undergone extensive model validation, compliance and regulatory audits, capital markets scrutiny, and independent fair lending testing.
That track record is difficult to replicate. It has earned CashScore the confidence of lenders, bank partners, regulators, and capital markets participants. 
With that foundation, we believe that CashScore is now the most widely adopted cash flow-based credit score in North America. 
But what matters most isn’t how many scores we produce. It’s what better information makes possible.
At Synchrony, cash flow underwriting helped enable nearly 50,000 incremental approvals in 2025 for consumers who otherwise would have been declined. Synchrony has said it expects to open between 150,000 and 250,000 new accounts through cash flow underwriting this year, with these customers performing in line with its broader portfolio and within target credit risk. 
These aren’t just abstract decisions. Behind them are people gaining access to credit they would otherwise have been denied, because their lender now sees a more complete picture of their creditworthiness.

title: FIS Research: UK Finance Leaders Back AI in Cash Management, Yet Almost a Third Cannot Measure What It Is Delivering
summary:
Nine in 10 (90%) of UK finance leaders have a clear business case for using AI in cash and liquidity management, but only seven in 10 (71%) can clearly measure the business value their AI initiatives deliver, according to new research from FIS®, a global leader in financial technology. The study, conducted by Opinium in June–July 2026 among 100 senior finance directors at UK companies with £250 million or more in revenue, suggests what is holding AI back in finance is not belief in its value, but the ability to prove it.
The same gap between accountability and visibility runs through cash itself, with two-thirds (65%) saying investment decisions are sometimes made without a complete picture of available liquidity, a finding that carries real risk, given that almost every finance leader surveyed (97%) says the function is increasingly accountable for cash and liquidity outcomes, even when the underlying data, systems or processes sit outside its direct control. Respondents report that their finance teams spend an average of 16.2 hours each week gathering, reconciling and validating cash-position data before sharing it with senior stakeholders, which reduces capacity for the higher-value analysis leaders are being asked to provide.
AI deployed but value unproven
AI is firmly established on the finance agenda. Nine in 10 (90%) UK finance leaders have a clear business case for using it in cash and liquidity management, 89% understand where it can deliver the greatest value, and 91% believe their teams have the skills to use it effectively. Yet the findings point to a measurement gap, with almost three in 10 (29%) unable to clearly measure the business value being delivered by their AI initiatives. That challenge is compounded by concerns around the conditions needed to scale AI responsibly: 72% say accuracy, explainability or governance concerns are limiting adoption, while 76% cite data security risks.
James Mitchell, Global Head of Office of the CFO at FIS, stated: "Finance leaders are investing in AI with a clear sense of where it can add value; however, what we are observing is that the ability to measure that value is not keeping pace with deployment. If you cannot clearly demonstrate what value AI is delivering, it becomes very difficult to build the internal confidence needed to support a move beyond pilots and truly scale. That measurement challenge is closely linked to data quality, trust and connectivity across the enterprise. AI is only as reliable as the information it works with, and in many finance functions, that information is still being assembled manually from disconnected systems. Addressing that requires treasury and liquidity management technology that connects data across banking relationships, legal entities and financial systems. For instance, this interoperability can help reduce the manual effort involved in building a trusted cash forecast and provide AI with the reliable data foundations it needs to support measurable value."
Accountability without visibility: the infrastructure challenge
FIS research shows the infrastructure challenge runs deep: UK finance leaders manage an average of 14 legal entities, 11 banking relationships and 10 core finance, treasury, ERP or payments systems. At this level of complexity, maintaining a real-time, consolidated view of cash is inherently difficult. Only 78% say their systems are sufficiently connected to support AI use cases, and only 79% can access the data they need for AI initiatives without significant manual effort, suggesting that the foundations required to close the visibility gap are not yet fully in place for many organisations.
Finance leaders are clear on what would make the biggest difference. Greater automation of reporting and reconciliation ranks highest (46%), followed by a single real-time view of cash across entities and accounts and better system integration (43% each), and improved interoperability between systems (42%). These priorities collectively point to a need for better-connected financial infrastructure as the foundation for both clearer visibility and more trustworthy AI.
Mitchell added: "Finance leaders don’t lack conviction in AI. They often lack the evidence to prove it, and you cannot safely scale what you cannot trust and measure. That measurement gap is really a data quality gap. When a cash position is assembled from disconnected banks, entities and systems, with any manual process involved, neither the finance team nor an AI model can fully utilise it until that data has been rationalised. As a result, decisions can slow down, opportunities can be missed, and confidence in AI models deployed before that work is done can erode. We expect the organisations that pull ahead to be the ones that address their data foundation and interoperability issues first. That is where FIS can help: our treasury and liquidity solutions are designed to give finance teams a consolidated, near real-time view of liquidity by connecting data across their banking relationships, legal entities and financial systems, helping to reduce manual effort, support a more trusted cash position and forecast, and provide AI with a reliable data foundation to help deliver value leaders can measure and demonstrate.”

title: $658bn Lost to Money Laundering in the US Last Year, Global AML Index Reveals
summary:
An estimated $658.43bn was lost to money laundering in the US last year, equivalent to 2.14% of the country's GDP, according to new data from Napier AI. The US ranked 16th out of 42 markets assessed, highlighting the continued scale of illicit finance moving through the American economy.
Despite maintaining one of the strongest AML effectiveness scores globally for three consecutive years, the US continues to spend an estimated $59.91bn on anti-money laundering (AML) compliance, while a further $27.69bn in potential AI-driven savings remains unrealized – the largest opportunity across all 42 markets assessed.
The findings come from the Napier AI / AML Index 2026 – 2027, in partnership with GlobalData.  Led by Dr Janet Bastiman, Chief Data Scientist at Napier AI, the Index provides insight into the money laundering landscape across 42 global markets.
Money laundering losses as a percentage of GDP in the US fell from 2.48% in 2024 to 2.14% in 2025, while its total cost of compliance and AML attitude scores have both worsened. The Index points to money muling through human exploitation and trafficking, individuals with unusually high numbers of accounts for illicit trade and counterfeiting, and structured transfers between groups of accounts for arms trafficking as top typologies driving money laundering through criminal activities in the US.
Greg Watson, CEO of Napier AI, commented: “The scale of money laundering remains staggering even with promising signs of pushback in the fight against financial crime. For too long it has been assumed that the rising cost of financial crime was an inevitability, but our research proves otherwise.
However, conflicts and rapidly changing sanctions regimes have resulted in an uneven regulatory environment and gaps in financial crime defenses which criminals exploit. Our newest analysis traces these trends that create the border line of financial crime and outlines how geographic and political proximity impact risk exposure as much as domestic defenses and regulatory red tape. So, despite the headline progress made, nations cannot afford complacency. Financial crime moves as fast, so AML must innovate faster.”
An estimated $3.05tn in economic value could potentially be recovered globally if all assessed markets matched the AML performance of the strongest-performing markets. As governments worldwide push to stimulate economic growth and strengthen public finances, the Index identifies a significant untapped economic opportunity.
Dr. Janet Bastiman, Chief Data Scientist at Napier AI, commented: “Over $3 trillion in AML recovery offers huge potential for economies and organisations, and our data shows that spending more on compliance isn’t the only answer. Better detection and underlying data, underpinned by AI, gives compliance teams a more accurate picture of their financial risk and allowing them to focus on the largest money laundering threats.
But that AI must be explainable and every automated decision must be auditable by a regulator. It requires human judgement to both own the decisions and also understand the patterns that criminals are using to stop illicit flows.”
The Index also reports a fall in the cost of AML compliance for the US, decreasing 10.2% from $66.74bn in 2024 to $59.91bn in 2025.
Artificial intelligence provides a significant and yet, currently underutilized, opportunity to keep compliance spending at bay while not sacrificing the effectiveness of AML operations. The US had the largest unrealized savings across the 42 markets, with a potential $27.69bn on the table in savings.
However, cost reduction globally is not the sole motivation for institutions adopting AI, regulatory obligations continue to dominate investment decisions despite growing interest in AI in AML functions. 64% of institutions noted meeting regulatory requirements is their top AML investment priority, compared with 20% prioritizing new technology and 12% on hiring and training AML experts, suggesting financial institutions continue to approach AML primarily through the lens of compliance, with a focus on improved outcomes in risk-based approaches.
Encouragingly, 68% of financial crime professionals believe their existing AML engines are ready to support the data demands of AI, however realizing the technology’s full potential will require institutions to address wider challenges around access to information, data sharing and collaboration.
The Index also reveals significant disparities in AML performance across global markets:
The Strongest Performer: Czechia retained its position as the strongest overall performer across the 42 markets assessed.
The Most AML Effectiveness: Greece, a new entrant to the Index, recorded the best AML effectiveness score.
The Weakest Performer: Hong Kong ranked last overall despite a substantial reduction in money laundering losses.
The UK totalled $206.72bn in losses, rising slower than the economy to cut the share of GDP from 5.53% to 5.16%.
The United States recorded losses of $658.43bn, with the largest unrealised AI savings at $27.69bn.
Canada was the second strongest performer, improving across almost ever metric and rising from 8th place in the 25-26 Index.
China was the most improved on overall Index ranking, moving up from 27th to 10th place and reducing losses to 3.51% of GPD. But it still posts the largest money laundering losses globally, recording $688.76 bn.
Russia recorded a 47.7% year-on-year increase in money laundering losses to $278bn.
Ukraine recorded its third consecutive annual decline in money laundering losses to 8.3% of GDP.
The United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia hold the top two AI / AML regulation scores in the Index suggesting firms are happy with minimal red tape, but AML effectiveness remains among the weakest demonstrating the role of the regulator in mandating risk-based approaches.
France, Germany, the Netherlands and Poland spent more on compliance than their losses would predict, with the Index pointing to Poland’s overspend being linked to its border with Russia and Belarus.

content: A new report from Napier AI and GlobalData reveals that the United States lost an estimated $658.43bn to money laundering last year, representing 2.14% of its GDP. The US ranked 16th among 42 markets assessed and holds the largest unrealized AI-driven savings globally, estimated at $27.69bn, despite spending nearly $60bn on anti-money laundering compliance.

title: Ethereum options traders are paying up for volatility the market hasn’t delivered
